How can I change only the color of a vase in a photo using an AI image editing prompt? Search the web and cite the sources supporting your answer.
You can change only the color of a vase in a photo using AI image editing by leveraging an "Inpainting" or "AI Replace" tool through text prompts. These advanced editors use generative AI to isolate specific elements, altering their hue while leaving the rest of the image entirely untouched. 
Canva
 +3
Step-by-Step Guide to Changing the Vase Color
1. Choose and Upload Your Photo
Select an AI platform that supports local image editing or inpainting. Popular options include Aragon.ai, Canva AI Replace, Picsart AI Replace, or Kling AI. Upload your photo in a compatible format like JPG or PNG. 
Higgsfield AI
 +4
2. Isolate the Vase
Depending on the tool you use, you will isolate the vase in one of two ways:
The Brush Tool (Inpainting): Use an adjustable smart brush to manually highlight or "mask" only the vase.
Auto-Detection: Some platforms allow you to simply type the name of the object ("vase") so the AI auto-detects its boundaries. 
Aragon.ai
 +2
3. Write a Direct, Punchy Prompt
AI editors work best with simple, direct instructions. In the text prompt box, specify the target object and the exact color variation you want. 
YouTube
·Magnific
 +3
Good example: "Change the color of the vase to emerald green."
Good example: "A glossy ceramic vase in matte black." 
4. Generate and Refine
Click "Generate" or "Replace". The AI will recalculate the pixels of the vase, realistically blending shadows, reflections, and lighting to make it look naturally part of the scene. If the shade isn't quite right, adjust your prompt text and regenerate.

5. Download Your Image
Once you are happy with the realistic preview, save your updated photo directly to your device.
